top.title: NLC, TUC feud: How we brokered peace in Ajaero, Osifo’s rift — Obiajulu
top.description: *lSays some individuals exploited situation to tear labour movement apart By Victor Ahiuma-Young The protracted disagreement between the leadership of the Nigeria Labour Congress, NLC, and the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria, TUC, over the Federal Government’s N70,000 transport relief agreement with the NLC, which the TUC rejected, threatened to undermine the unity and collective bargaining strength of organised labour. The disagreement escalated into public exchanges and personal attacks between NLC President, Joe Ajaero, and his TUC counterpart, Festus Osifo, raising concerns that the welfare and interests of Nigerian workers were being overshadowed by the leadership crisis. Worried that the feud could further divide the labour movement and weaken its ability to defend workers’ interests, veteran labour leaders, led by pioneer NLC President, Hassan Sunmonu, intervened and brokered peace between the two leaders. Other prominent figures involved in the reconciliation included Dr Peace Obiajulu, Comrades Peter Esele, Ayuba Wabba, Bobboi Kaigama and Quadri Olaleye. In this interview, former TUC President, Dr Obiajulu, recounts what triggered the crisis, how it escalated, and how the intervention of the labour elders helped restore cordial relations between the two labour centres. She reveals that poor communication largely fuelled the disagreement, while some individuals exploited the situation, warning that the crisis nearly tore the labour movement apart and ultimately put workers’ interests at risk. What actually led to the disagreement between the Nigeria Labour Congress and the Trade Union Congress, and how did you get involved in the reconciliation? To start with, I was not even aware that there was a disagreement between the two organisations. I was called by Quadri Olaleye, a former President of TUC. He told me that the President of NLC had asked whether Mrs Obiajulu, whom we fondly call Mummy, had been informed about the meeting. That was when I asked whether there was a problem between TUC and NLC. He said yes. I responded that it was a family matter, just like disagreements between a husband and wife or among children in a family. In all honesty, I do not know who initiated the reconciliation process. I am sure it was the elders. They must have seen what was happening on television and read about it in the newspapers. If I had come across the situation myself, I would equally have reached out to some of the elders to intervene. I would not like to see organised labour become a target of public ridicule. The moment TUC and NLC begin to quarrel or fall apart, workers are left on their own. Whenever there is a problem within the labour movement, workers are the ones who suffer because nobody will be left to speak effectively on their behalf. How serious had the disagreement become before the elders intervened? If there is a disagreement between NLC and TUC, workers ultimately bear the consequences. top.title: Texas women's basketball: Longhorns roll past Southeastern Louisiana to a 7-0 start
top.description: Isi Etute of the Texas Longhorns looks to pass the ball while defended by Lucia Navarro of the Tarleton State Texans during the second half Nov. 14, 2026 at Moody Center in Austin. (Scott Wachter/Getty Images) This Thanksgiving, the Texas women's basketball team can be thankful for an undefeated start to its season. Texas got double-digit point totals from six different players in Wednesday's 96-45 win over Southeastern Louisiana at Moody Center. With the win, the sixth-ranked Longhorns improved to 7-0 against a schedule that has featured four opponents that qualified for the 2026 NCAA Tournament. More: Subscribe to the Statesman's Texas sports newsletter Texas has yet to trail in a game this season, and the Longhorns weren't in danger of facing that first deficit on Wednesday night. Fueled by an early 15-0 run, Texas seized a 23-5 lead by the end of the first quarter and took a 34-point lead into halftime. A Southland Conference representative, Southeastern Louisiana (2-5) trailed by as many as 55 points in the second half. Sophomore guard Jayda Clark and freshman forward Isi Etute respectively scored 19 and 18 points to lead the Longhorns. Texas also got 14 points, 10 assists and six steals from All-American forward Madison Booker . Starting guard Zya Vann missed Wednesday's action with an undisclosed injury. top.title: Risk of retaining fuel subsidy outweighed political consequences – Idris
top.description: • President misrepresented on electricity supply promise – Onanuga •FG defends power sector reforms, increased revenue to states By Juliet Umeh MINISTER of Information and National Orientation, Mohammed Idris, has defended President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms, saying the removal of fuel subsidy and unification of exchange rates saved Nigeria from imminent economic collapse. Idris, who spoke at an interactive session with journalists organised by the All Progressives Congress, APC, Presidential Campaign Council Media and Strategic Communications team in Lagos, Monday, said the President took politically risky decisions in the overriding interest of the country. He maintained that the reforms had improved government revenues at all levels, strengthened the economy and positioned the country for sustainable growth. He said: “When the President took office in May 2023, there were two major policy decisions. One was doing away with this monster called fuel subsidy. The second was ensuring that the multiple exchange rate regimes that we had in this country were also done away with. “Presidents after presidents, everyone knew that fuel subsidy was a big problem and a big drain on the economy of this country. But no one was able to achieve its removal until President Bola Tinubu came. “It was not a convenient decision for Mr President. In fact, it was politically risky for him, for someone who had just won an election, who had just been sworn in and who had another election staring him in the face.” Idris explained that the administration considered the consequences of retaining the subsidy and concluded that delaying the reforms would have been more damaging to the country. “The risk of waiting any longer far outweighed whatever political risk he, as a person, as a president or as a politician, should take. “This created enough fiscal headroom, not just for the Federal Government but also for the sub-nationals. Federal Government has made a lot more money. Sub-nationals have made a lot more money,” he said. Economy on path to recovery The minister also said international financial institutions and rating agencies had acknowledged improvements in Nigeria’s economic outlook. He said: “The IMF, the World Bank, everybody is saying, yes, we have some challenges as a nation, but our economy is on the path that will lead us to prosperity. “Our GDP is on the rise. Inflation that was becoming a big problem has been curtailed. Headline inflation, food inflation, all are down.” However, journalists at the meeting raised concerns over persistent insecurity, high petrol prices, inadequate electricity supply, distribution of Compressed Natural Gas, CNG, buses and the impact of increased allocations to state governments on citizens’ welfare. top.description: OKLAHOMA CITY — As the final seconds ticked away, Kenrich Williams had a chance to make it a one-point deficit with seconds to go. After missing, Ajay Mitchell had the same chance. He also missed from the outside. The two most consequential shots of the night once again fell short. The Oklahoma City Thunder didn't have enough fourth-quarter firepower in their 113-106 loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves . This was part of the 2026 NBA Cup West Group B play. Changing up the starters once again, the Thunder couldn't solve their slow starts. They were in a 26-16 deficit after the first quarter. Offense continued to be a problem for short-handed OKC as it fell behind by double-digit points. Fueled by Alex Caruso's defensive energy, the second unit did a lot better to open the second frame. The Thunder exploded for 37 points in the second frame. Quite the juxtaposition from the opening frame. That included a 20-8 run. Gilgeous-Alexander drilled a stepback 3-pointer on Jaden McDaniels' grill. Caruso took on LaMelo Ball as the primary defender to gum up Minnesota's fast-paced offense. After such a strong second quarter, the Thunder had a 53-47 halftime lead over the Timberwolves. All things considered, that was a great spot to be at. Minnesota has been one of the hottest teams since Anthony Edwards went down with knee surgery. Meanwhile, OKC has been reeling with a ton of similar-looking losses piling up. Like usual, the wheels started falling off for the Thunder in the second half. Ball went on a heater with circus-looking jumpers. OKC's once-indestructible defense looked mortal. Actually, scratch that — detrimental. The Timberwolves ballooned for 40 points in the third frame. That made OKC's 30-point frame an afterthought. top.description: Mandatory Credit: Thomas Shea-Imagn Images The Houston Rockets picked up an impressive 116-104 victory over the Phoenix Suns , but the star of the show was Alperen Sengun . The Houston big man delivered a historic performance with 23 points, 11 rebounds, and 11 assists, recording a triple-double while passing Hakeem Olajuwon in the franchise record books (2nd in franchise history in triple-doubles). It was another reminder of how special Sengun has become in the best season of his career so far. Sengun wasn’t alone, though. Kevin Durant finished with 20 points and 10 rebounds, while Amen Thompson added 18 points, 10 rebounds, and four assists. Jabari Smith Jr. and Fred VanVleet contributed 13 points apiece, giving Houston five starters in double figures. The Rockets controlled the glass, winning the rebounding battle 51-38 and collecting 20 offensive rebounds. They also moved the ball effectively, finishing with 30 assists. Phoenix struggled badly from the perimeter, making just 5-32 three-point attempts (15.6%), which made it difficult to keep pace despite Devin Booker ‘s 25 points and Jalen Green ‘s 16-point contribution from the backcourt. Houston’s biggest concern was its free-throw shooting. The Rockets made just 16-30 attempts, leaving plenty of points at the line. Fortunately, their rebounding advantage, balanced scoring, and Sengun’s historic night were enough to secure the 12-point victory. top.title: 'We needed to take that risk!' - Bruno Fernandes reveals half-time tactical switch behind Manchester United's Lisbon turnaround
top.description: TOPSHOT-FBL-EUR-C1-SPORTING-MAN UTD - AFP Bruno Fernandes inspired a fierce second-half turnaround with two goals in three minutes as Manchester United drew 2-2 away to Sporting CP in the Champions League. Named Player of the Match, the United skipper explained how aggressive pressing rattled Sporting after half-time before late drama denied Mauricio Pochettino his first win. Fernandes leads United's rapid second-half response Bruno Fernandes dragged Manchester United back from a frustrating first half with two goals inside three minutes after the interval, though Mauricio Pochettino had to settle for a 2-2 Champions League draw against Sporting CP. Trailing to Luis Suarez's 33rd-minute penalty after Amad Diallo's header was ruled out for a foul by Youri Tielemans, United struck back through Fernandes' 48th-minute spot-kick and a deflected long-range strike two minutes later. "I wanted to win the game. It was very important for us to win because of our position in the Champions League, but it was also important not to lose," Fernandes told UEFA after receiving the Player of the Match award. "It's very tough to play here at Alvalade, with the great atmosphere created by the fans and a very good team." Explaining the high-pressing shift against Paulo Fonseca's side United struggled to break down Sporting's high defensive line before the interval, with Joshua Zirkzee firing off target on his first start since May and Bryan Mbeumo crowded out. However, Fernandes revealed a bolder pressing approach after the break transformed the contest. "We came back very strong in the game because we could put some intensity into pressing high. We need to take that risk sometimes, playing one-on-one and having more people in front," he explained. "As Sporting want to play from the back, sometimes when you are very aggressive, you can recover some balls and get into a good position." Late errors, VAR heartbreak and a fair verdict Fernandes nearly completed a quickfire hat-trick when a free-kick flew just wide, before goalkeeper Senne Lammens spilled Ivan Fresneda's 80th-minute cross to gift Suarez an equaliser. United saw a late Kaique own goal disallowed by VAR for a foul and lost Tielemans to a second yellow card in stoppage time. Reflecting on Paulo Fonseca's tactical setup, Fernandes admitted a share of the spoils was justified: "The way Paulo Fonseca set his team up against us was different. We knew they would play a high line, which forced them to take risks, but at the same time made it difficult for us to reach the final third and get the ball in behind. Overall, I think it was a very good game, and the draw was a fair result." top.title: Tinubu vows to sustain peace, defeat insurgency in North-East
top.description: •Promises rescue of abducted Askira Uba schoolchildren •Shettima, Zulum hail security gains, seek second term for Tinubu ABUJA — President Bola Tinubu has pledged to sustain the relative peace recorded in Borno State and the North-East, directing security agencies to intensify operations against fleeing insurgents. Tinubu, who spoke yesterday at an All Progressives Congress, APC, rally in Maiduguri ahead of the 2027 general elections, said the security gains achieved by the armed forces would be consolidated and translated into full economic recovery. In a statement by his spokesman, Bayo Onanuga, the President commended Borno State Governor, Prof. Babagana Zulum, for restoring hope and transforming the state’s economy. “Let me start by thanking the Governor of the State, Prof. Babagana Zulum. Well done on restoring Borno State and transforming its economy. “You restored our hope by believing that stability will bring development,” he said. Tinubu, who commissioned projects including the National Youth Service Corps Female Lodge and Borno International Conference Centre, said the North-East had witnessed economic improvements in the last three years, with increased investments in education, healthcare and infrastructure. top.title: 10 Classic Books Worth Reading Over and Over
top.description: Most of us treat classic literature like a checklist to conquer in high school or college and then never touch those books again. You power through the plot, underline a few quotes for a term paper, and move on to whatever else is new. The catch is that great books rarely reveal their most fascinating tricks on the first pass. When you already know the ending, your brain stops racing for answers and begins to notice the machinery holding all those mysteries and themes together. Suddenly, an unreliable narrator's sleight of hand becomes obvious, or a throwaway line in chapter two hits like a freight train in light of later developments .

nigeria.title: Nigeria Joins Global Pact To Protect Marine Biodiversity, Unlock Ocean Resources
nigeria.description: Nigeria has secured a significant international milestone for the country’s marine and blue economy, following its formal ratification of a landmark United Nations treaty on the conservation and sustainable use of marine biodiversity in areas beyond national jurisdiction. The historic instrument of ratification was deposited on behalf of President Bola Tinubu by Nigeria’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Jimoh Ibrahim, at the United Nations Headquarters in New York. ﻿ Speaking at the ceremony, Ibrahim highlighted the economic and strategic importance of the agreement to Nigeria, noting that it would expand the country’s opportunities to benefit from ocean resources through greater participation in the governance of the high seas. The Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ) Agreement, also known as the High Seas Treaty, provides a framework for the protection, management and sustainable use of marine resources in areas beyond national jurisdiction. For Nigeria, a coastal nation along the Gulf of Guinea, the agreement marks a significant step towards strengthening its marine economy, protecting biodiversity, supporting fisheries and unlocking opportunities in emerging ocean-based industries. A major implication of the ratification is Nigeria’s plan to develop a proposal for the establishment of a highly protected marine area on the high seas. The initiative is also expected to strengthen efforts to conserve marine ecosystems while promoting the fair and equitable sharing of benefits from ocean resources, particularly for developing countries. Nigeria signed the BBNJ Agreement on May 3, 2024. Following the deposit of its instrument of ratification, the agreement will enter into force for Nigeria on December 24, 2026. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Strategic Bitcoin Reserve Bill Clears House Committee, Heads to Floor A bill that would write the U.S. Strategic Bitcoin Reserve into federal law is now eligible for a vote on the House floor, after the House Financial Services Committee formally reported it on Tuesday. The American Reserve Modernization Act of 2026, H.R. 8957, was filed with amendments as House Report 119-894 and placed on the Union Calendar as Calendar No. 789 on Nov. 24, according to congressional records. The committee had voted 28-21 to advance the bill at a Sept. 16 markup. Rep. Nick Begich, an Alaska Republican, introduced the bill on May 21. It now lists 23 cosponsors, including Rep. Jared Golden, a Maine Democrat, with Reps. Byron Donalds and Maria Elvira Salazar of Florida added on Nov. 24. What the amended bill does The reported text directs the Treasury secretary to set up a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve and a separate Digital Asset Stockpile within 180 days of the law taking effect. Bitcoin owned by the federal government would move into the reserve, while other digital assets would go to the stockpile. The centerpiece is a lock-up. Treasury would have to hold all bitcoin deposited in the reserve for at least 20 years after enactment, and during that period no reserve bitcoin could be “sold, swapped, auctioned, encumbered, or otherwise disposed of for any purpose.” After the 20 years, the Treasury secretary could recommend selling up to 10% of the reserve in any two-year period. Two years before the holding period ends, Treasury would have to send Congress recommendations on whether to keep holding or begin a gradual release. Federal agencies would have 60 days after enactment to give Treasury a full accounting of the bitcoin and other digital assets they hold or have seized. Until the reserve is set up, agencies could not sell those coins except for national security, when required by law or a court, or to return assets to crime victims. The bill also creates a Proof of Reserve system. Treasury would publish an annual report on total holdings, transactions and control of private keys, checked by an independent auditor with expertise in cryptographic attestations, while the Government Accountability Office would provide oversight. States could choose to store their own bitcoin in segregated accounts inside the federal reserve, keeping title to the coins and the right to withdraw them. People from 121 countries and territories applied to speak, attend or screen their work, and more than 19,000 people joined the programme in person and online, as EWA streamed its sessions live for the first time. Over the six days, more than 150 speakers led nearly 100 panels, masterclasses, workshops, roundtables and podcast sessions, while around 50 films were screened across the week. The celebrations began on Opening Night at the Livespot Entertarium, where guests were treated to an evening of music, fashion, film and comedy to mark five years of EWA. Sixteen emerging artists performed in front of a room of industry leaders, creatives and partners, and the night featured an exclusive 30-minute screening of University of Side Hustle, the first scripted feature film from Livespot Studios , written by Dami Elebe and executive produced by Deola Art Alade . By day, EbonyLife Place hosted a packed programme across seven tracks: Film & TV; Music; Fashion & Beauty; AI & Tech; Art & Animation; Live Events & Production; and Creative Enterprise. Nissi Ogulu led a masterclass on animation as Africa’s next big storytelling frontier, and From Lagos to Disney explored what it takes to bring African stories to global screens. Creators picked up practical tips in sessions with Victoire, Ifeoma Udeme and Canva. Other sessions tackled sync licensing, music funding, building Africa’s touring circuit and turning creative skills into businesses. The podcast stage kept the energy going with live recordings of CreativiTea and Crea8torium , which closed the final day. Fashion took over the Entertarium for The Runway Coterie, an evening of bold collections that ended with the announcement of the EWA Fashion Lab winners after a week-long programme with mentors. Hooked By Lade won first place with ₦2 million, Estaz took second place and ₦1 million, and Melira placed third, winning ₦500,000. Lush Hair styled the runway as the show’s hair sponsor. Next door, the EWA Art Floor invited guests into The Spaces Between Us , an exhibition that blended photography, painting, installation, archival work, fashion and live performance. Curated by Jumoke Sanwo and produced with Revolving Art Incubator (RAI) as it celebrated its tenth anniversary, the exhibition featured work by 21 Nigerian artists and seven fashion designers. entertainment.title: Nollywood Legend Pete Edochie Passes Away at 79
entertainment.description: Nollywood icon Pete Edochie, MON, who passed away at the age of 79 in Enugu. Photo Credit: Pete Edochie/Instagram Nollywood and the wider African entertainment community are mourning the loss of one of their most respected screen icons, Pete Edochie , MON, who passed away on Wednesday, 25 November 2026,at the age of 79. According to an official statement released on behalf of the family by his eldest son, Leo Pete Edochie , the veteran actor and retired broadcaster departed this life at 12:30 a.m. in Enugu, Nigeria, following a protracted battle with prostate cancer. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. At age 20, in 1967, he joined the Eastern Nigeria Broadcasting Service (ENBS)—later the Anambra Broadcasting Service (ABS)—rising steadily through the ranks to serve as Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. His defining breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed the fierce, tragic hero Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s (NTA) acclaimed television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart. His commanding presence and deep, resonant voice earned him international recognition—including a dedicated delegation interview from the BBC—and cemented his place in Nigerian television history. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). In recognition of his immense contributions to Nigerian arts and culture, he was conferred with the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003 by former President Olusegun Obasanjo,alongside the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards (AMVCA) Industry Merit Award and lifetime achievement honours from the Africa Film Academy and the African Film Festival (TAFF). entertainment.title: How Williams Alamu Graduated with First-Class Honours in Statistics from the University of Ibadan
entertainment.description: Williams Alamu marks his B.Sc. First-Class Honours graduation in Statistics from the University of Ibadan. There was a time when Williams Alamu would rather not sit an examination than risk getting a grade he wasn’t happy with. A B or a C in his Cambridge A-levels felt like a possibility he wasn’t ready to entertain, so he didn’t write the exams. A few years later, at 23, he has graduated from the University of Ibadan with a B.Sc. in Statistics, First-Class Honours and a CGPA of 3.65/4.0. Somewhere along the way, he decided that fear was no longer going to make his decisions for him. When Williams got into UI, he had a rather ambitious plan: become the Best Graduating Student in his faculty. Getting there would require more than good intentions. There were 5:30am wake-ups, difficult Statistics courses, friends who became unofficial tutors, a ChatGPT Pro subscription in 300 level, job offers he turned down and one Demography exam that kept him awake for 36 hours. University, as it turns out, came with quite a few plot twists. In this interview with BellaNaija, Williams takes us through the habits, people and decisions that shaped his academic journey. He also tells us whether he got that coveted top spot, what he learnt from the opportunities he put on hold, and what he would tell another student hoping to graduate with First-Class Honours. If that’s a goal you’re working towards, you may want to take notes. Literally or otherwise. Williams Alamu celebrates graduating with First-Class Honours in Statistics from the University of Ibadan. At what point did you realise you were chasing a record-breaking grade? Was it a goal from Day 1, or did it evolve? It was a goal from day one, actually. When I gained admission into the University of Ibadan, I already had my mind set on graduating as the Best Graduating Student in my faculty. I knew becoming the overall Best Graduating Student in the university would require an extraordinary amount of work, but I felt being the best in my faculty was something I wanted to work towards. And, of course, that would also mean graduating as the best student in my department. The motivation behind that goal goes back to shortly after secondary school, when my parents enrolled me in a Cambridge A-level programme. I went into it hoping to achieve three A-stars, but Chemistry was a major struggle. As the examinations approached, I became increasingly worried about my performance. I think I was more afraid of not meeting my own expectations than I was of the examination itself. entertainment.title: Solape Fayemi Launches Saina Properties Across Four Markets
entertainment.description: For many people, buying property is one of the biggest financial decisions they will ever make. Yet, knowing who to trust, how to verify ownership and whether a property is worth the investment can make the process overwhelming. It is a challenge Solape Fayemi hopes to address with the launch of Saina Properties , a real estate company now operating across Nigeria, the United Kingdom, the United States and the United Arab Emirates. Officially unveiled at an event held on 17 November at the Marriott Hotel, Ikeja GRA, Lagos, Saina Properties is built around a simple idea: property ownership should be guided by sound advice, proper verification and professional support, not just the excitement of closing a deal. For Solape, whose experience in the investment industry shaped her understanding of money, risk and wealth creation, the decision to establish the company came from recognising the need for a more considered approach to real estate. “We are not building Saina Properties because the world needs another company selling properties. We are building Saina because we believe there is room for a different kind of real estate experience. One where advice comes before the transaction, where due diligence is not treated as an inconvenience, and where people are encouraged to ask questions, understand their options and make informed decisions,” she said at the launch. That philosophy is reflected in the company’s three core areas of expertise: Advisory & Verification, Sales & Brokerage, and Developments . Rather than focusing solely on connecting buyers to properties, Saina brings together the guidance investors need to assess opportunities, the support required to navigate property transactions, and involvement in real estate development. The company is also building on experience gained before its official launch, having supported more than 25 clients with property opportunities across different markets. An important part of its proposition is the role of professional expertise in protecting property investors. Fayemi’s position raises a familiar question: people consult doctors for medical concerns and lawyers for legal matters, so why do some investors leave significant property decisions in the hands of relatives simply because they are available or familiar with the location? While trust and family relationships matter, they do not automatically translate into the technical knowledge needed to assess a property, verify its documentation or understand its investment potential. These decisions require proper checks, market understanding and accountability. With its operations spanning four markets, Saina Properties aims to support individuals and investors looking to navigate property ownership with greater clarity, whether they are buying, selling or exploring development opportunities. entertainment.description: Chef Soliat Bada Anyone who grew up in a Nigerian home knows the line. You suggest buying food outside, and before you finish the sentence, someone reminds you that there’s rice at home. It is usually the end of the conversation. In Asali Africa’s new series, it is where the conversation starts. There’s Rice at Home is a cooking and conversation show from Asali Africa, the Lagos-based creative development agency, hosted by Chef Soliat Bada . In each episode, Soliat cooks one rice dish with a guest, and while the pot does its work, the two get into the kind of talk that usually happens around food: family, money and what success really looks like. Rice is the most ordinary thing in a Nigerian kitchen, and the show makes a good case that it doesn’t have to taste ordinary. Over five episodes, released every two weeks, the menu travels from Jamaica to Saudi Arabia, back home to Nigeria and on to Louisiana. You don’t just watch the food get made, either. The recipes are written up in full on Asali Africa’s website, with the ingredients and method laid out step by step, so you can watch Soliat cook a dish and then make it in your own kitchen. The season opens with Rice and Peas with Oxtail, the Jamaican Sunday staple of rice cooked in coconut milk with red kidney beans (the “peas”), served beside rich, slow-cooked oxtail. Soliat’s guest is Michael Famoroti , co-founder of Stears, and their conversation turns to family and black tax: the expectation that once you start earning, you start supporting the people who raised you. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? sports.title: 'We needed to take that risk!' - Bruno Fernandes reveals half-time tactical switch behind Manchester United's Lisbon turnaround
sports.description: TOPSHOT-FBL-EUR-C1-SPORTING-MAN UTD - AFP Bruno Fernandes inspired a fierce second-half turnaround with two goals in three minutes as Manchester United drew 2-2 away to Sporting CP in the Champions League. Named Player of the Match, the United skipper explained how aggressive pressing rattled Sporting after half-time before late drama denied Mauricio Pochettino his first win. Fernandes leads United's rapid second-half response Bruno Fernandes dragged Manchester United back from a frustrating first half with two goals inside three minutes after the interval, though Mauricio Pochettino had to settle for a 2-2 Champions League draw against Sporting CP. Trailing to Luis Suarez's 33rd-minute penalty after Amad Diallo's header was ruled out for a foul by Youri Tielemans, United struck back through Fernandes' 48th-minute spot-kick and a deflected long-range strike two minutes later. "I wanted to win the game. It was very important for us to win because of our position in the Champions League, but it was also important not to lose," Fernandes told UEFA after receiving the Player of the Match award. "It's very tough to play here at Alvalade, with the great atmosphere created by the fans and a very good team." Explaining the high-pressing shift against Paulo Fonseca's side United struggled to break down Sporting's high defensive line before the interval, with Joshua Zirkzee firing off target on his first start since May and Bryan Mbeumo crowded out. However, Fernandes revealed a bolder pressing approach after the break transformed the contest. "We came back very strong in the game because we could put some intensity into pressing high. We need to take that risk sometimes, playing one-on-one and having more people in front," he explained. "As Sporting want to play from the back, sometimes when you are very aggressive, you can recover some balls and get into a good position." Late errors, VAR heartbreak and a fair verdict Fernandes nearly completed a quickfire hat-trick when a free-kick flew just wide, before goalkeeper Senne Lammens spilled Ivan Fresneda's 80th-minute cross to gift Suarez an equaliser. United saw a late Kaique own goal disallowed by VAR for a foul and lost Tielemans to a second yellow card in stoppage time. Reflecting on Paulo Fonseca's tactical setup, Fernandes admitted a share of the spoils was justified: "The way Paulo Fonseca set his team up against us was different. We knew they would play a high line, which forced them to take risks, but at the same time made it difficult for us to reach the final third and get the ball in behind. Overall, I think it was a very good game, and the draw was a fair result." United sit 19th as Pochettino searches for first victory Having suffered defeat at Anfield on Sunday before Wednesday's chaotic stalemate in Lisbon, Pochettino remains in search of his maiden victory as Manchester United manager. sports.title: 'Maybe I need to move here!' - Anthony Gordon jokes about relocating to Azerbaijan after firing Champions League brace for Barcelona against Sabah FK
sports.description: FBL-EUR-C1-SABAH-BARCELONA - AFP Anthony Gordon ended his month-long goal drought with a clinical brace as Barcelona defeated Sabah FK in the Champions League at the Baku Olympic Stadium. Having now scored six goals across two Champions League visits to Azerbaijan, the England forward joked he might need to relocate there while admitting he should have claimed a hat-trick. Gordon ends goal drought with clinical brace in Baku Anthony Gordon fired two goals to help Barcelona justify their status as heavy favourites with a commanding Champions League victory over Sabah FK at the Baku Olympic Stadium. Having won the starting spot on the left wing ahead of Karim Adeyemi since arriving last summer, the England international finally added end product to his high-intensity pressing by striking in the 30th and 50th minutes—capitalising on rebounds from goalkeeper Pokatilov on both occasions while seeing another effort disallowed after a VAR review. Having last scored for Barcelona against Alaves on October 31, Gordon joked about his remarkable affinity for Azerbaijan after netting four times there for Newcastle United against Qarabag last season. "Maybe at some point in my life I need to move here! I've been very successful here, and yeah, great game today. Obviously two goals, so I'm happy, but potentially could have had a hat-trick, so still a lot of work to do," Gordon told Stan . Missing a hat-trick and overcoming a gruelling journey Asked after full-time whether six goals in two seasons made him the "King of Baku", Gordon played down the title while ruing a missed left-footed chance for a treble. He also praised Barcelona's collective focus after a long trip away from home. "I wouldn't say that, but it's a very special place for me. I should have scored a hat-trick, but I missed that one with my left foot. I'm very happy," he explained. Reflecting on the squad's display, Gordon added: "I think it was very good because, like I said, it's really difficult to travel. We came here two days ago to come away from family and have this kind of experience, but Azerbaijan is a beautiful place." Chasing Harry Kane's English Champions League benchmark Gordon's double lifted his tally to three goals in five Champions League appearances this season, having also netted against Galatasaray. Across his career, he now boasts 13 goals in his first 23 Champions League proper outings—a record among English players surpassed only by Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane, who scored 18 in his first 23 appearances. Before making way for Raphinha in the 76th minute, Gordon registered five shots (three on target), an 84% pass completion rate and two ball recoveries as Barcelona blew Sabah away with three goals inside 10 second-half minutes. It goes without saying that I won't include obvious calls like "start Trey McBride" or "sit Tommy DeVito." A win would go a long way towards getting their momentum back. A loss would sap any kind of energy from the win the other night. Let’s go to the tape. As is often the case, the Blue Jackets come out of the gate with speed, and this was no different here, as they came with an initial push that forced the Devils to stay sharp in the first few minutes. Eight minutes into the game, the Devils did not have a shot on goal, and the Blue Jackets already had six. At 8:06, though, the Devils finally got a shot in on Cam Talbot who left a rebound out front. Nico Hischier was there and opportunistic, shoveling home the rebound, to give the Devils a 1-0 lead! At this point, the Devils started to settle in and get more pucks on Talbot. But Brenden Dillon would make a strong appearance, taking a match penalty with a brutal hit on Denton Mateychuk. sports.title: ‘Suspend him’ – NFL fans want consequences for Rams DB Karen Kinchens after hit on Christian Watson
sports.description: Photo by Kevin Terrell/Getty Images Los Angeles Rams DB Karen Kinchens’ tackle on Green Bay Packers WR Christian Watson has led to plenty of reactions from fans on both sides. The Rams and Packers have been in the midst of a heated Wednesday Night Football clash on November 25 to set up the NFL Thanksgiving Weekend. The tone for the big game weekend has been set with a gritty and physical clash between the Rams and Packers. However, it seems the physicality might have gone a little too far during a second-quarter moment which ended with Kinchens tackling Watson, leading to the Packers WR leaving the game with a concussion. NFL fans cringe after watching Karen Kinchens’ hit on Christian Watson The play came with two minutes left in the second quarter on a 4th & 1. Packers QB Jordan Love found Watson near the touchline, who caught the pass and was instantly levelled by a brutal hit from Kinchens. Fans seem split on how serious the tackle was, with many calling it dirty and expecting consequences for Kinchens, while others are calling the backlash soft. “Suspend him for the rest of the season,” said one Packers fan . “I hope everything is okay, man. —- bro… Praying for everything to be straight with you, Watson. That Kamren dirty… Smh,” said another fan calling Kinchens dirty . “That was a hard but clean hit. Clearly,” said one fan defending the hit . “They need to eject his ass immediately. That is completely uncalled for and unacceptable. He was well on his way out of bounds!” were the thoughts of another fan . “Absolutely horrible call and horrible ejection,” said another fan, thinking the reaction to the play was a bit too much. Kinchens was ejected from the game after the tackle, while Watson was placed in concussion protocol. The Rams secured this win behind an incredible performance from RB Blake Corum. Kinchens registered one assisted tackle and two passes defended before his ejection, while Watson had 65 yards and one TD on four receptions during the game. sports.title: Rams lean on Blake Corum's 184 yards and a strong defense to defeat Packers
sports.description: Green Bay Packers safety Javon Bullard dives to pursuit of Rams running back Blake Corum in the fourth quarter of the Rams' 26-13 win Wednesday night at SoFi Stadium. (Allen J. Schaben / Los Angeles Times) The stadium rocked. The crowd roared. The players delivered big hits. And that’s just what happened during legendary rock band U2’s halftime performance of the Rams ’ game against the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday night at SoFi Stadium. Before and after, the Rams put together perhaps their most important effort of the season in a 26-13 victory . Blake Corum rushed for a touchdown and a career-best 184 yards, Kyren Williams rushed for a touchdown and the Rams’ defense forced three turnovers as the Rams improved their record to 7-4 . Rams linebacker Byron Young sacks Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love in the fourth quarter Wednesday. (Allen J. Schaben / Los Angeles Times) Corum, who turned 26 on Wednesday, carried the ball a career-high 32 times and eclipsed 100 yards rushing for the second consecutive game. Brandon McManus kicked four field goals. The Rams, the preseason Super Bowl favorite, had stumbled to a 2-4 start. But they have now won five games in a row. The previous four came against the Las Vegas Raiders, Chargers, Washington Commanders and Arizona Cardinals, none of which have winning records. But the matchup against the Packers was different, and it carried huge postseason implications. The Packers (6-5) are in the hunt for a playoff spot out of the NFC North, where the Detroit Lions (8-2), Chicago Bears (8-2), and Minnesota Vikings (7-3) are also battling for postseason berths. Now the Rams have the head-to-head tiebreaker if the Rams and Packers end up with the same record at the end of the regular season. Rams running back Kyren Williams scores on a seven-yard touchdown run in the second quarter against the Packers on Wednesday. (Allen J. Schaben / Los Angeles Times) The Rams have games remaining against the Kansas City Chiefs (8-2), the NFC West-leading San Francisco 49ers (9-1), the Dallas Cowboys (5-6) and two games against the defending Super Bowl-champion Seattle Seahawks (6-4) sandwiched around a trip to play the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-7). With receiver Puka Nacua out for the season and Davante Adams still on injured reserve, second-year pro Konata Mumpfield stepped up and caught four passes for 69 yards. Quarterback Matthew Stafford completed 16 of 23 passes for 140 yards, with an interception. KEY TAKEAWAYS: Mumbai Indians ' auction purse has dropped by ₹2.35 crore, from ₹32.60 crore to ₹30.25 crore. The revision is linked to retention-slot valuation after Hardik Pandya's departure. MI's four retained capped players have a combined slab value of ₹61 crore, above their actual salaries. MI will enter the IPL 2027 mini-auction with ₹30.25 crore and nine slots to fill. Explained: Why MI's IPL 2027 auction purse reduced by ₹2.35 crore after BCCI revision The Mumbai Indians' purse for the upcoming IPL 2027 mini-auction has been cut down to ₹30.25 crore due to the revision of the purse value by the BCCI. The five-time champions were initially allotted ₹32.60 crore after the retention and release list , but their revised purse value in the mini-auction was declared to be ₹30.25 crore on November 25 . This revision in purse has led to confusion among the people regarding the reason behind such an occurrence since all the nine other teams have retained their purse values from the time of their retention and release list. MORE: IPL 2027 auction player pool: Initial register, overseas players and deadline Why has Mumbai Indians' purse been reduced by ₹2.35 crore? This reduction is related to the valuation of MI's retained players under the IPL's retention-slot rule, in light of Hardik Pandya's transfer to Punjab Kings (PBKS). Initially, Mumbai used the sum total of the salaries of the four remaining capped players that are, Jasprit Bumrah, Rohit Sharma, Suryakumar Yadav and Tilak Varma. The salaries of the aforementioned players are ₹18 crore, ₹16.30 crore, ₹16.35 crore and ₹8 crore, respectively, which adds up to ₹58.65 crore. But the IPL's retention rule requires teams to consider the cost of retention slots for the players, as opposed to simply adding up the salary cost of the players. Accordingly, with respect to the new calculation rule, the four retained capped players of MI have been evaluated at ₹61 crore. Consequently, the difference between the two valuations comes out to be ₹2.35 crore. technology.description: The United States Federal Communications Commission has approved SpaceX’s plan to launch a million datacenter satellites. The regulator on Wednesday published an order [PDF] allowing SpaceX to operate a “Non-geostationary satellite orbit (NGSO) constellation of 1,000,000 satellites deployed into orbital shells each spanning 50 km at altitudes from 500 to 1,002 km and in 30-degree inclinations and sun-synchronous inclinations.” The order requires SpaceX to ensure its satellites’ radios don’t interfere with US government systems which use the 28.6-29.1 GHz band and requires the company to stick to operating within the parameters it files with the International Telecommunications Union. SpaceX asked the FCC to waive its rule requiring the atmospheric disposal of dead satellites orbiting at 2,000 km or less. Elon Musk’s company asked for “flexibility to dispose satellites operating above 600 km altitude into Earth disposal orbits or heliocentric orbits.” The FCC found SpaceX did not provide enough information to let it assess if proposed “alternative disposal methods” are compliant with regulations, so deferred its decision on the waiver request. “SpaceX must file an application for modification of this authorization and provide sufficient justification for any requested waiver(s) of the Commission’s rules,” the order states. The company must also file twice-yearly reports about “conjunction events” – moments when its satellites get dangerously close to each other, or other orbiters. Whether orbiting datacenters are feasible, make sense, or will ever pay for themselves, remain open questions. Analyst firm Gartner has described the idea as “ peak insanity .” Google thinks orbiting datacenters become viable if launch costs fall to $200/kg, which would mean SpaceX needs to launch its massive Starship 1,800 times. SpaceX’s assumptions assume near-daily launches, far better than its current cadence of a launch every three days or so. Fundamental networking research must also come to fruition to handle the amount of traffic large constellations of orbiting datacenters will create. Terrestrial manufacturing capacity will also need to increase to build all those satellites. Elon Musk’s companies and Intel have planned a giant new fab to make that possible, without explaining how the supply chains behind chip manufacturing will scale to make it feasible. That's a notable omission given that semiconductor supply chains are already extremely strained. Approval for SpaceX is therefore nice but in no way a roadmap to a million datacenter satellites. Google, ironically, is a little further along than SpaceX, having launched a test sat in October and last week announcing it has hired Amazon founder Jeff Bezos’ Blue Origin to launch a larger satellite carrying the equivalent of a full datacenter rack in early 2029. technology.description: Four years ago, NASA dispatched a small spacecraft on a suicide mission to show how humanity might deflect an asteroid on a collision course with Earth. Using telescopes, astronomers measured changes in the orbit of Dimorphos around a larger asteroid companion named Didymos in the aftermath of NASA's Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) mission. The spacecraft released some 10 billion joules of energy as it impacted Dimorphos in September 2022 at more than 13,700 mph (6.14 kilometers per second), shortening the asteroid's 12-hour orbit around Didymos by about 33 minutes, 25 times the most conservative expectation. technology.title: The security of US water systems is even leakier than we thought
technology.description: American water systems are even less secure than we thought, according to a study of 236 technology vendors that provide gear to US drinking water, wastewater, and industrial water systems. The federal government has issued 4,014 security advisories for industrial control systems and cataloged 1,792 vulnerabilities known to have been exploited in cyberattacks. A new index, called Water Supply Chain Watch and published by exposure management firm Securin, however, found almost twice as many vulnerabilities as public records identified – including 20 exploited flaws that weren't even in the federal government's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog. The security provider compared data on water-tech vendors with records from the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), the FBI, and WaterISAC, drawing on CISA advisory data through November 20 and KEV catalog entries through November 23. It found that federal water advisories hit their highest level this year since 2020. However, the volume of security alerts isn't a reliable predictor of real-world attacks, the researchers noted. Five vendors – Rockwell Automation (58), Advantech (48), Schneider Electric (35), Siemens (26), and ABB (24) – account for 191 of the 376 water-tagged security advisories. The No. 2 firm, Advantech, accounted for the highest number of vulnerabilities rated critical, but none of the CVEs in its advisories appear in CISA's KEV catalog. Unitronics, on the other hand, accounted for only two water-tagged security advisories, but at least 75 of its controllers were compromised between November 2023 and January 2024 by attackers taking advantage of default or missing passwords. The report also highlights another disconnect between water-related CVEs and real-world cyberattacks, which don't always require attackers to exploit software bugs. The July intrusions, which security researchers suspect were the work of Iran-linked attackers , targeted more than 100 water systems , with incidents reported across at least 12 states , and involved poorly secured internet-connected controllers . According to Securin, 791 Rockwell MicroLogix 1400 controllers across multiple industries in the US were exposed to the internet as of November 17. Additionally, research by Forescout cited by the security shop found that most exposed Rockwell controllers in the US – seven in 10 – sit on mobile carrier networks, where poorly secured cellular modems can provide an entry point for attackers. A CISA advisory from July describes this technique: The authoring agencies observed Iranian-affiliated APT actors using several foreign-based IP addresses to access internet-facing PLCs manufactured by Rockwell Automation/Allen-Bradley, Schneider Electric, Siemens, and potentially other manufactured PLCs [ T0883 ]. technology.title: Huawei and crew tout homegrown EDA tools to overcome China’s fab deficit
technology.description: Chinese telecom and IT giant Huawei boasted about its advancements in domestic electronic design automation (EDA) software this week, which it needs to accelerate the adoption of homegrown chip manufacturing. EDA is an umbrella term for software, hardware, and services essential to the planning, design, and production of modern chips. Today, Cadence Design Systems, Synopsys, and Siemens dominate the industry, but US export controls have restricted Huawei and other blacklisted Chinese businesses' access to their tools. The US blacklisted Huawei back in 2019 over concerns the telecommunications equipment giant could be forced to inject backdoors into its gear. Unable to access top EDA tools, Huawei’s chip division, HiSilicon, was forced to develop its own with the help of Phlexing Technology. This week, Phlexing chairman Qing He detailed the company’s efforts to bring new EDA tools to support Huawei’s so-called Tau Scaling Law design philosophy. “Tau EDA is the domestic EDA tool chain for Tau chips. It comes from a long, close partnership with Huawei,” he said. We discussed the tech earlier this year, but in a nutshell, it involves using advanced packaging, specifically 3D hybrid bonding, to achieve higher transistor density for a given area. The TSMC of China, Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation (SMIC), is still years behind Taiwan, South Korea, and the US on process technology. It currently has the ability to mass-produce chips on the equivalent of a 7 nm process. For comparison, TSMC began producing 5 nm-class products in 2020 and commenced mass production of 2 nm-class chips in late 2025. So, Huawei aims to use 3D packaging to close the gap, but for this to happen, it first needs tools capable of designing such chips, and that’s just what Phlexing claims to have done with its GloryBolt and GloryEX platforms. “Traditional EDA has long handled only single processes. Tau EDA needs to integrate and decompose multiple processes,” He said. “Coupling multi-scale, multi-structure, and multi-physics issues called for new analysis tools.” This, He says, culminated in the co-development of a process design kit (PDK) with Huawei beginning in 2024. These technologies have now gone live. The development comes as Huawei looks to bring larger, more capable processors to market. We previously discussed the company’s latest developments around AI accelerators, near packaged optics, networking, and rack systems. Many of these advancements will depend on multi-die chip packages, enabled by EDA tools, like those built by Phlexing. ®

technology.description: Note: At the time of writing, I was unaware of criticism directed at Ladybird creator Andreas Kling’s public statements. Readers interested in this background can find further context in accounts by Kelson Vibber and Drew DeVault . After four years of work to build a browser engine from scratch, the Ladybird project released its first downloadable alpha on November 23, offering prebuilt versions for macOS and Linux. Previously, curious users had to compile the browser themselves from its source. Now it's an installable package with automatic updating. Ladybird is most notable for what it isn't: another browser fork. Where Chrome, Edge, Brave, and Opera all run on Google's Blink engine, and Firefox depends on Gecko, Ladybird's rendering engine and its LibJS JavaScript engine were written from scratch. "The engine is our own, built from the ground up, and not a fork," project lead Andreas Kling wrote in Monday's announcement. "The browser around it is modest, but functional." science.title: December full moon 2026: When, where and how to see the Cold Moon
science.description: null The December full moon reaches peak illumination at 8:28 p.m. EST on Dec. 23 (0128 GMT on Dec. 24) as the lunar disk shines opposite the sun in Earth's sky. It is often called the "Cold Moon" in reference to the frigid temperatures that prevail in the Northern Hemisphere around the time of its rising, according to the Old Farmer's Almanac . December's full moon will also occur close to perigee — the moon's closest point to Earth in its elliptical orbit — giving rise to a spectacular supermoon. A supermoon can appear 30% brighter and 14% larger than a full moon at its farthest point from Earth (also known as a micromoon).. According to the late, great astronomer Fred Espenak , the Cold Moon will be just 221,667 miles (356,740 kilometers) from Earth when it turns full, making it the closest supermoon of 2026! When to see the December full moon The full Cold Supermoon will make for a spectacular sight when it rises over the eastern horizon at sunset on Dec. 23, mere hours before reaching maximum illumination. Remember to use Time and Date's moonrise and moonset tracker for timings specific to your location. Earth's satellite may appear larger than normal while close to the horizon. This is partly because it is near perigee, when it appears subtly larger in the night sky, but also because of a phenomenon called the moon illusion, which tricks us into perceiving the moon to be bigger than it actually is while in the presence of foreground objects. A yellow full moon rises over Italy. (Image credit: Photo by Lorenzo Di Cola/NurPhoto via Getty Images) The moon may also adopt a striking golden or orange hue around moonrise and moonset. When the moon is low on the horizon, its light travels through more of Earth's atmopshere, scattering shorter, bluer wavelengths of light and allowing longer, redder wavelengths to reach our eyes. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 25, 1970: NASA's 'wingless' M2-F3 'lifting body' aircraft makes its 1st powered flight ahead of supersonic tests
science.description: null On Nov. 25, 1970, an experimental aircraft called the Northrop M2-F3 made its first powered flight. The M2-F3 aircraft was a heavyweight "lifting body" designed to test its ability to produce most of its lift through its fuselage instead of wings. It's commonly referred to as a "wingless" aircraft. After Air Force test pilot Bill Dana took the M2-F3 on three unpowered glide test flights, he did the first powered flight, too. Dana soared to an altitude of 45,000 feet during this flight, which lasted just over 6 minutes. He didn't break the sound barrier this time, but he did on later flights. The M2-F3 flew a total of 27 missions in its three-year flight history. Its top speed was 1.6 times the speed of sound, and its top altitude was 71,500 feet. NASA's M2-F3 lifting body drops from its carrier plane during a test flight in 1970. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered In the late 1960s and early 1970s, NASA was investigating lifting bodies as an approach to both new aircraft and what future spacecraft, and as its number suggests, the M2-F3 was not the first of its kind. In fact, the M2-F3 was a rebuilt version of its predecessor, the M2-F2 lifting body , after that vehicle crashed in a dry lake bed in California's Mojave Desert during an unpowered test flight. That crash (which appears in the opening of the TV show "The Six-Million-Dollar Man") led to upgrades for a better handling lifting body, NASA said. "When the M2-F2 was rebuilt and redesignated the M2-F3, it was modified with an additional third vertical fin – centered between the tip fins – to improve control characteristics," NASA wrote in an overview . Unpowered glide flights for the M2-F3 began in June 1970, but Dana's flight on Nov. 25 of that year was the first time the vehicle fired up its rocket engine to test its controls under powered flight. One vital upgrade on the vehicle was a set of reaction control thrusters to help maintain its orientation. "A reaction jet control system, similar to thrusters used on orbiting spacecraft, was also installed on the M2-F3 to obtain research data about their effectiveness for vehicle control," NASA wrote . "As the M2-F3’s portion of the lifting body program neared an end, it evaluated a rate command augmentation control system and a side-arm control stick similar to side-arm controllers now used on many modern aircraft." If you want, you can see the M2-F3 vehicle today. NASA donated it to the Smithsonian Institution. It is now hanging at the National Air and Space Museum in Washington, D.C. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

science.description: NASA’s Office of Small Business Programs (OSBP) hosted a ceremonial Mentor-Protégé Agreement signing between The Boeing Company and GRACE Aerospace on Oct. 29, 2026, at the U.S. Space and Rocket Center in Huntsville, Alabama. As part of the program, NASA announced its latest Mentor-Protégé Agreement, this one signed between The Boeing Company and GRACE Aerospace. NASA is streamlining the application process for the Small Business Supplier Development Program, as well as reducing administrative requirements, accelerating review and approval timelines, and enhancing incentives for prime contractor participation. These improvements are aimed at making supplier development more accessible, efficient, and closely aligned with NASA’s mission needs. “We have intentionally redesigned the program as a mission-focused tool for strengthening industrial base readiness and mission success,” said Dwight Deneal, assistant administrator, Office of Small Business Programs, NASA Headquarters in Washington. “By simplifying participation and focusing developmental assistance on the capabilities NASA needs most, we are helping build a stronger, more resilient supplier base that can support the agency’s highest-priority missions.” Under the new Mentor-Protégé Agreement, Boeing will provide structured assistance to help GRACE expand its capabilities as a supplier of mission-critical aerospace hardware. Boeing will fund the agreement, valued at nearly $500,000. “Boeing is proud to continue its longstanding relationship with NASA in support of its mission and the opportunities this agreement creates for Boeing, GRACE, and the broader aerospace industrial base,” said Christian Diamond, Mentor-Protégé Program manager and small business liaison officer for Boeing. “Through this partnership, Boeing looks forward to sharing our expertise to support the continued growth and long-term success of a small business while strengthening our supplier base.”

science.description: A northern gannet ( Morus bassanus ) tagged with biologging devices on its back and tail Steve Votier Audio from seabirds fitted with mini recording devices and GPS trackers has been used by researchers to show that marine life can record encounters with vessels that are otherwise difficult to track. Many large vessels are now legally required to carry automatic identification systems broadcasting their identity and location at regular intervals. Although this has allowed interactions between animals and fisheries to be studied at scale, there are enormous gaps in coverage. In fact, recent research suggests that three-quarters of industrial fishing vessels don’t use the technology, says Jonathan Rutter at the University of Oxford. This is partly because regulations on the types of vessels that are required to share data vary by country. Large satellite ‘blind spots’ also contribute to the problem, he says, and so does subterfuge for the purpose of illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing (IUU). The team analysed audio collected from devices attached to seven northern gannets ( Morus bassanus ) and found that one third of the audio detections couldn’t be matched with vessel tracking data – mostly off the UK coast. Overall, 12 per cent of the vessel detections made by the four critically endangered Balearic shearwaters ( Puffinus mauretanicus ) included in the study couldn’t be matched to public data. But given the high vessel density where they were – off the Catalan coast – the researchers estimated that up to 20 per cent of the vessels detected by the four birds weren’t broadcasting their identity. Tammy Davies at BirdLife International – a global partnership of non-governmental organisations – who wasn’t involved in the study, says the research could “give us a more complete picture of the risks seabirds face at sea” and “ultimately, this could contribute to better assessments of bycatch risk and help identify fisheries and areas where conservation measures are most needed”. Peter Ejbye-Ernst at the Netherlands Institute for the Study of Crime and Law Enforcement (NSCR), describes the study as “fascinating” from a green criminology point of view, too. science.title: SpaceX Starship debris becomes art in Ashley Zelinskie's 'The Weight of Space' (video, photos)
science.description: null When a SpaceX Starship broke apart over Turks and Caicos in Jan. 2025, pieces of its heat shield washed ashore. Some of that material now hangs on a gallery wall in New York City, embedded in artist Ashley Zelinskie's print of the very explosion it survived. Look closely at the print and you can see little flakes on the surface. Some of Zelinskie's friends vacationing on the islands had come across pieces of heat-shield tile. "I think you might want these," Zelinskie recalled one friend telling her. She did. The Brooklyn-based artist ground the fragments into dust and worked them into the print. Ashley Zelinskie incorporated dust from recovered SpaceX Starship heat-shield tiles into this print of the vehicle breaking apart over Turks and Caicos. (Image credit: Ashley Zelinskie) The Starship print is part of "Ejecta," which captures rocket plumes and explosions on paper. It's one of four series in Zelinskie's solo exhibition, "The Weight of Space," which opened Nov. 20 at Heft Gallery in Manhattan. Her marble sculptures in "Monuments" depict the Hubble Space Telescope, retired NASA astronaut Mike Massimino's spaceflight gear and more. Five "Launch Sequence" sculptures follow a rocket through liftoff, and the interactive "Crowded Sky" lets visitors track what's currently orbiting overhead in real time. Zelinskie gave Space.com Editor-in-Chief Tariq Malik and me a tour before the gallery doors opened. Massimino joined her that evening to celebrate the exhibition and their collaboration on "Monuments." You can watch the tour in the video above. science.title: Green light for Starmind: SpaceX gets approval to deploy 1 million AI satellites
science.description: null Earth orbit could get a lot more crowded in the coming years. The U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) just granted SpaceX approval to deploy one million of its Starmind AI data-center satellites in orbit. "This action opens a bold new frontier for the computing infrastructure needed to power America's leadership and growth," FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said today (Nov. 25) in a statement announcing the approval. AI has become central to SpaceX's business plans and identity over the past year or so. For example, the company has said that it's eyeing a "total addressable market" of $28.5 trillion over the long haul — and nearly $23 trillion of that is in "enterprise AI applications." Starmind is key to those lofty ambitions. SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk believes that the future of AI compute is in space, where energy (from the sun ) is unlimited and there are no land-owning neighbors to lodge NIMBY complaints. SpaceX aims to launch the first of its Starmind satellites in the third quarter of 2027. The spacecraft will fly on the company's fully reusable Starship megarocket, which has deployed 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink satellites on its most recent two test flights . Those 52 spacecraft are the vanguard of another enormous constellation: Musk has said that the next-gen Starlink network will eventually consists of about 100,000 satellites . The planned numbers for Starlink and Starmind are truly mind-boggling. To put them into perspective: Since the dawn of the space age in 1957, humanity has launched a total of just 28,000 satellites, give or take a few hundred. And the biggest constellation ever operated to date, the current iteration of Starlink, consists of about 11,000 spacecraft. These coming buildouts will require an enormous number of launches. Starship can carry a maximum of 60 V3 Starlink satellites per launch, for instance, so it will take about 1,700 liftoffs just to assemble that network (and more to maintain it, as the operational life of each satellite is expected to be about five years). Putting so many satellites into orbit also raises the risks of collisions. SpaceX has proven to be extremely proficient in this regard with its current Starlink satellites, which can detect and avoid potential collisions autonomously. But more evasive maneuvers will be required as space gets more and more crowded. SpaceX isn't the only company that aims to operate data centers in space; Cowboy Space , Starcloud, Blue Origin and Google, among other companies, have voiced similar ambitions. Starcloud and Google , in fact, have already launched AI pathfinder satellites. "Compute campuses or data centers are essential to sustaining America's leadership in SI," Carr said in the same statement. science.title: AI’s stunning progress in maths shows how little we understand it
science.description: MARK SYKES/SPL/Alamy There is a story, possibly apocryphal, that when the mathematician G. H. Hardy was about to undertake a dangerous sea voyage, he sent a postcard to a colleague declaring “I have solved the Riemann hypothesis”. Hardy, a staunch atheist, joked that this would prevent his ship from sinking, as God would never let him claim the credit for such a major result without revealing the details of his proof. Hardy would probably be both astonished and aghast that we now have what seems to be a proof of the Riemann hypothesis , a problem that has vexed mathematicians since the 19th century, but that no one yet understands it. The consensus among mathematicians is that the proof, produced with the aid of AI, will hold, but that it will take much more work to make it comprehensible to humans. However you feel about AI, this is a watershed moment, and one that demonstrates just how little we still understand about the capabilities of the technology. As recently as last month, leading mathematician Terence Tao speculated that AI would eventually solve the Riemann hypothesis, but that it may not happen before 2050. Now, some mathematicians are considering whether their hardest and most infamous remaining problems could be settled within months. In a year that has left mathematicians reeling, this may be the knock-out blow. Advertisement This is a watershed moment, and it shows just how little we understand about AI’s abilities For non-mathematicians, the fall of the Riemann hypothesis is harder to interpret. In the past year, AI has seen incredible advances in both maths and coding, but it is perhaps no coincidence that in these arenas, with nothing more than computer code, answers can swiftly be checked and iterated upon, allowing for rapid improvement. When it comes to other human endeavours though, from art to zoology, such verification is far harder, involving either the messy physical world, or unknowable human taste – or both. Whether this verification gap can be closed may become the biggest question of our age. Answers on a postcard, please. What is the Riemann hypothesis and why is its solution so monumental? It has been called the hardest problem in mathematics, and now through a combination of human ingenuity and relentlessness, and the computational power of AI, the Riemann hypothesis may have finally been solved

science.description: The New Scientist Book Club read Chris Beckett’s Dark Eden in November Since starting the New Scientist Book Club in May 2023, I have aimed to vary our books as much as possible, moving between science fiction and popular science, older classics and the hottest new titles. Occasionally, though, I’m afraid I let the power go to my head and just choose one of my own personal favourites. That’s what I did in November, with Chris Beckett’s novel Dark Eden , a book I’ve loved ever since it won the Arthur C. Clarke award in 2013. Set on the planet Eden, a sunless world that drifts alone far outside the Milky Way, this follows the descendants of two astronauts who were marooned there over a century earlier. Now numbering 532 people, they tell each other stories of the world their ancestors came from, and struggle to survive on this dark, cold planet as they await the return of “one of those sky-boats with lights on them”. I think it is all wildly imaginative and original and exciting. So it was with some trepidation that I awaited the verdict of my fellow book club members on our Discord channel. I really wanted everyone else to love it, too! Free newsletter Sign up to Book Club Sign up to newsletter It started well. “I managed not to stay up all night reading, but the temptation was definitely there – I am hooked,” wrote Dee55. Les was similarly gripped. “Started it? I’ve only gone and finished it, haven’t I? It really got me in, and I found it a fascinating exploration of social anthropology and linguistics in a very small, isolated population. And the world-building was fascinating, too – very different flora and fauna.” Advertisement Several other members also cited the strength of the world-building in Dark Eden . I also love the lanternflowers and woollybucks of this planet, and was fascinated to learn, in an essay Chris wrote for book club members, that, when creating a world for a story, he doesn’t “usually seek to make the whole thing scientifically accurate, but I try to make it hang together in a way that feels coherent”. I think he definitely succeeds in that here. In Dark Eden, I imagined how life might exist on a sunless planet Dark Eden, the November read for the New Scientist Book Club, takes place on a rogue planet outside the Milky Way. science.title: Is The Time Traveler’s Wife the perfect audiobook to experience on shuffle?
science.description: Josie Ford Feedback is our weekly column of bizarre stories, implausible advertising claims, confusing instructions and more Reader Jenny Ozanne writes to tell us of a horrific incident that befell her partner. He had bought Audrey Niffenegger’s novel The Time Traveler’s Wife as a CD audiobook, to listen to on long car journeys. “After a while, he complained that the plot was completely impossible to follow,” writes Jenny. “It was only when I checked his player that I realized he had accidentally set the CD to ‘shuffle’. “ Advertisement Jenny raises two points, which Feedback heartily endorses: “I’m still not sure what’s more impressive: the story’s ability to survive total chronological chaos, or the fact that he listened to three random chapters before suspecting anything was wrong.” Feedback would suggest that The Time Traveler’s Wife might be the ideal novel to experience on shuffle, since the narrative is heavily non-linear. The main character hops uncontrollably back and forth through history. This led us to wonder: would any similarly chrono-displaced stories survive the experience of being played on shuffle, or even be improved by it? We wondered, for instance, about David Mitchell’s Cloud Atlas . This has six stories set in different periods, including a future in which human clones are used as cheap labour, and a more distant future in which everything has gone a bit Mad Max . The stories are linked by characters in later timelines reading about the earlier ones, and by subtle coincidences. What would it be like on shuffle? However, after careful reflection, we realised there is only one correct answer to this, and that is Shane Carruth’s 2004 film Primer , which tells the story of two tech bros who invent a time machine in their garage. At first, they use it to go back in time and make money on the stock exchange, only to become caught up in an escalating web of betrayal and deception as they endlessly rewrite their lives. Primer is so overcomplicated, so mind-wreckingly confusing, that some poor soul once went so far as to draw a diagram trying to convey its timeline. Posted on Reddit by u/Clawz114, the diagram looks like a cross between a metro map and a flowchart of the inner workings of a chemical factory. It is therefore possible that playing the scenes in random order might actually cause the film to make more sense. The last refuge of the true gift scoundrel is, of course, the scented candle. This item might as well come with a note saying, “Sorry, I couldn’t think of anything”.
